## Excursions to Tigre and the Paraná Delta: which itinerary to choose

[Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) lies north of [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) amid the rivers, channels and islands of the Paraná Delta. The cityscape gives way to jetties, wooden houses beside the water and green riverbanks. It is an easy addition to a stay in the Argentine capital if you want to experience the region's waterways.

We offer **three different excursions** connected with Tigre. Two depart from Buenos Aires via its northern neighborhoods, while the third focuses on the delta and includes lunch. Compare their durations, guide languages and included services rather than relying on their similar names.

## Three Tigre excursion options

| Program | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [Tigre in 4 hours](/argentina/buenos-aires/tigre-delta-tour-from-buenos-aires/) | Trip from the capital, boat ride, San Isidro |
| [Tigre and the Northern Zone](/argentina/buenos-aires/tigre-northern-buenos-aires-tour/) | 6 hours, English-language guide |
| [Tigre and the Paraná Delta with lunch](/argentina/tigre/tigre-parana-delta-half-day-lunch/) | Half day, guide, tickets and lunch |

The first two programs have a confirmed starting price of **$100**, although their lengths and terms differ. The price of the half-day option with lunch is confirmed separately. It should not be assumed to have the same rate just because all three visit Tigre.

## Tigre in 4 hours: a short excursion with a river cruise

The [four-hour tour from Buenos Aires](/argentina/buenos-aires/tigre-delta-tour-from-buenos-aires/) travels through San Isidro to Tigre. It includes a tourist boat ride along the waterways of the delta. Along the way, you can see island shores, waterfront houses and characteristic buildings in the capital's northern suburbs.

The description names San Isidro, the presidential residence Quinta de Olivos and a historic rowing club. **Transport and guiding services are included**; lunch is extra. This is an option for travelers who want to devote part of a day to Tigre and leave time for other plans in the capital.

The excursion costs $100. This figure belongs to the terms of that particular excursion and should not be applied to the other products.

## Tigre and the Northern Zone: a longer outing

The ["Tigre and the Northern Zone" excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/tigre-northern-buenos-aires-tour/) lasts **6 hours**. It also passes through San Isidro and Tigre, introduces the capital's northern suburbs and includes an outing on the delta.

The excursion has an **English-speaking guide**. Transfers and guiding are included; lunch is not. The original price is $100.

Choose this option if you want more time in the northern metropolitan area and are comfortable with an English-speaking guide. Even though its base price is the same as that of the four-hour product, the included services should not be assumed to be identical: compare each program separately.

## Half a day with a guide, tickets and lunch

The ["Tigre and Paraná Delta: half-day excursion with guide and lunch"](/argentina/tigre/tigre-parana-delta-half-day-lunch/) focuses on the waterways and life along the town's riverbanks. The confirmed inclusions are a guided half-day excursion, tickets under the itinerary, lunch and transfers as specified.

Drinks are paid separately unless a different arrangement is agreed. Having lunch included is convenient if you prefer a predefined set of services. However, the exact vessel type and full list of stops must be confirmed for this excursion: the tourist boat from another program should not automatically be considered part of this one.

## What is the Paraná Delta like?

The delta is a network of islands, rivers and narrow channels. Its waterways form a transport network for residents: passenger boats use them, goods are delivered along them and people reach their island homes by water. Even a short excursion shows how closely everyday life is linked to the river.

For visitors, the primary experience is the view from the water. Beyond the city are jetties, overgrown banks, holiday homes and permanent residences. With a longer stay in Tigre, you can also stroll along the waterfront. Treat additional museums, markets and restaurants as separate options unless they are explicitly listed as part of the chosen excursion.

## Choosing by time and interests

If you have around half a day and want an excursion from Buenos Aires with a boat trip, compare the [four-hour route](/argentina/buenos-aires/tigre-delta-tour-from-buenos-aires/) with the [half-day program including lunch](/argentina/tigre/tigre-parana-delta-half-day-lunch/). The former explicitly includes a boat and the northern suburbs; the latter includes lunch and tickets under its own itinerary.

If you want to spend more time in the northern neighborhoods and are happy with English, consider the [six-hour excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/tigre-northern-buenos-aires-tour/).

For the delta, bring sun and rain protection, comfortable shoes and insect repellent. The climate is humid and conditions on the water may feel different from the city. Allow time to reach the departure point and return to Buenos Aires.

## Frequently asked questions about Tigre excursions

### How far is Tigre from Buenos Aires?

The town is roughly 40 km from the capital. Actual travel time depends on the departure point and traffic. Check each product for its full excursion duration: four hours, six hours or half a day.

### Are there excursions with lunch?

Yes. Lunch is included on the [half-day Tigre and delta itinerary](/argentina/tigre/tigre-parana-delta-half-day-lunch/). On the four-hour and six-hour excursions, lunch is paid for separately.

### Do all excursions include a river cruise?

A boat ride is explicitly described on the two itineraries through the northern suburbs of Buenos Aires. The third focuses on the delta and its scenery, but the vessel type and water-based portion must be checked against the confirmed program.

## Half-day Tigre and Paraná Delta excursion with lunch

In [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/), north of Buenos Aires, urban streets meet a network of channels in the Paraná Delta. Boats travel between islands and houses stand along the banks with their own jetties. The scenery is very different from the Argentine capital's broad avenues.

Our half-day excursion explores **Tigre and the Paraná Delta**. Confirmed inclusions are guiding services, admission tickets under the itinerary, lunch and transfers. The exact format of the water section and list of stops should be agreed for the specific group: the route introduces the waterways and riverside life, while the vessel and details of travel along the channels need confirmation.

## Understanding the Paraná Delta

The delta was formed by sediment carried by the Paraná River before it reaches the Río de la Plata system. Deposits create islands and sandbanks, with numerous rivers and channels separating the land. Unlike a typical urban neighborhood, island life here depends directly on water transport.

The municipality of Tigre's official tourism portal describes more than 350 rivers and streams in the delta. Boats serve not only sightseers but also island residents and goods transport. From the water, you can see jetties, waterfront homes and the vegetation typical of humid lowlands.

The excursion is interesting precisely because it combines natural scenery with everyday life. Among the channels are small residential buildings, wooden shoreline structures and dense greenery. This is a different kind of nature observation from a wildlife safari intended to encounter particular animals.

## Attractions in Tigre itself

Tigre is a gateway to the delta's waterways, but the town also has attractions of its own. They include historic rowing clubs, museum buildings, waterside promenades and the well-known Puerto de Frutos, a former fruit-trading port that has become a market for crafts and other goods.

Buenos Aires' official tourism portal describes Puerto de Frutos as a place to find wooden and wicker products, furniture, local foods and souvenirs. However, a visit to this market **is not confirmed** as a required stop on Ada Tours' standalone excursion. If you particularly want to visit the market or a museum, arrange it separately.

That distinction matters when choosing a trip: a general visit to the delta introduces the region, while a detailed exploration of museums and markets requires additional time.

## How the half-day visit works

The Ada Tours program is described as a **guided half-day excursion with lunch**. Transfers and tickets under the agreed itinerary are included. Drinks are extra unless otherwise agreed.

| Part of the journey | Confirmed arrangement |
|---|---|
| Exploring Tigre | Half-day excursion format |
| Nature | Delta landscapes and daily life |
| Assistance | Guide and transfers under the program |
| Food | Lunch; drinks extra |

"Half day" does not automatically specify a particular amount of time on the water. The itinerary does not confirm a specific boat, departure pier or price for an independent catamaran trip. These details must be agreed when arranging the excursion if the water route is your main objective.

For group travelers, agree in advance on your priority: an overview of the town, a longer cruise through the channels or a combination of both. The more land-based stops you add, the less time remains for the delta.

## Weather and practical preparation

Weather in the delta affects navigation and the experience of the excursion. Strong winds, rain and water levels can change access to individual channels. If the agreed itinerary includes a boat segment, confirm the vessel type, dock, departure time and safety procedures.

Wear comfortable shoes and light seasonal clothing, and bring rain protection. For a trip on the water, plan how to protect cameras and belongings. For a large group, check the transport's capacity and whether everyone can be accommodated together.

The delta is best experienced at a leisurely pace. Birds and other animals can be found here, but the Ada Tours program does not guarantee sightings of particular species. The main appeal is the network of waterways, islands and the relationship between local people and the river.

## How Tigre differs from a Buenos Aires city excursion

A [Buenos Aires sightseeing excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-half-day-lunch/) focuses on architecture, historic avenues and city neighborhoods. Tigre reveals the natural geography surrounding the capital: islands, jetties and channels.

It is better to devote different parts of your trip to these two experiences. If you want to combine both in one day, allow for travel time. Tigre is outside central Buenos Aires, and the half-day excursion has its own program, lunch and transfers.

For more nature-focused travel, see [Argentina trips for wildlife and nature](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/). Compare the actual number of stops and excursion formats, not just attractive photographs.

## The excursion on an Ada Tours six-day itinerary

The [six-day "Argentina: Buenos Aires, Tigre and Gaucho Traditions" tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/) includes Tigre on **day 3**. In the morning, travelers leave with their guide for the Paraná Delta. Dinner at a local restaurant, with transfers, is included in the evening program.

The half-day excursion and the evening dinner are separate parts of the overall day. Do not assume that both meals or all the services of the six-day tour are automatically included in the standalone excursion. The standalone product includes one lunch, guide services, tickets and transfers.

Day 2 of the group tour includes a [Buenos Aires sightseeing excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-half-day-lunch/) and a [Michelangelo tango show](/argentina/buenos-aires/michelangelo-tango-dinner-transfer/), followed later in the journey by a trip to Uruguay and an introduction to gaucho traditions. Tigre adds the watery landscapes north of the capital to the experience.

## Frequently asked questions about the Tigre excursion

### How long is the Tigre excursion?

Our excursion lasts **half a day**. The exact departure time, duration of the boat portion and stops are agreed at booking.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Lunch is part of the half-day excursion. Drinks are paid for separately unless otherwise agreed.

### Is a catamaran trip compulsory?

The current standalone product confirms an introduction to the waterways and delta, but does not specify a particular type of vessel. Confirm the format and duration of the water portion before booking.

### Which is better: Tigre or a Buenos Aires sightseeing excursion?

Choose the city excursion for the capital's architecture and history. Choose Tigre and the Paraná Delta for islands, channels and waterside life. The two complement each other well on the [six-day Argentina tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/).

## Tour including a Tigre and Paraná Delta excursion

About an hour from [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the urban scenery gradually gives way to islands, channels and houses along the banks. [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) is one of the main starting points for exploring the Paraná Delta. Waterways connect island communities, while promenades and jetties reveal a different side of everyday life in the region.

Our [half-day "Tigre and Paraná Delta" excursion](/argentina/tigre/tigre-parana-delta-half-day-lunch/) is included in the **["Argentina in 6 Days: Buenos Aires, Tigre and Gaucho Traditions" tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/)**. It suits travelers who want to discover the landscape around the capital as well as its architecture.

## How the day in Tigre is arranged

The excursion is scheduled **for day three** of the six-day tour. In the morning, guests travel to Tigre and explore the Paraná Delta with a guide. **Tickets and lunch are included.** Dinner at a local restaurant, with transfers, is scheduled for the evening after returning.

This lets you spend the first part of the day among river channels and devote the evening to food and relaxation. The exact route within the delta, the length of each stop and the vessel type depend on the specific excursion arrangements. "Half day" does not mean that the excursion covers the entire delta.

| Time of day | Program |
|---|---|
| Morning | Guided [Tigre and Paraná Delta](/argentina/tigre/tigre-parana-delta-half-day-lunch/) |
| Daytime | Lunch included in the excursion |
| Evening | Restaurant dinner and transfers |

The half-day excursion includes the transfers specified in the program, a guide, tickets and lunch. **Drinks are excluded from the inclusions** unless agreed separately. The dinner is part of the multi-day tour, not the standalone half-day excursion.

## How the delta differs from Buenos Aires

A visit to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) usually focuses on historic neighborhoods, squares, landmarks and evening cultural programs. The Paraná Delta offers a different landscape: low green islands, water dividing into many branches, and riverside life very different from city streets.

Tigre's tourist and residential districts sit alongside jetties. According to Argentina's national tourism portal, the delta is popular for boat trips, visits to Puerto de Frutos market and waterside recreation. These activities are available in the region, but **they should not automatically be treated as separate stops on this particular excursion module**. Our excursion introduces Tigre and the delta; it does not cover every local attraction.

Combining the capital with the delta appeals to first-time visitors to Argentina: in just a few days, you can experience city life and river landscapes without traveling far north.

## What else is included in the six-day journey?

The ["Argentina in 6 Days" tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/) brings together several distinct experiences. Alongside the Buenos Aires sightseeing program are evening cultural activities and the Tigre excursion; subsequent days include other regional experiences, such as learning about gaucho traditions.

Tigre stands out among these stops for its natural scenery. If you are seeking an active multi-day river cruise, this half-day outing provides only an introduction to the delta. If the goal is a first visit to Argentina with several different experiences, it fits well alongside the city days.

Unlike a two- or three-week trip, this is a compact journey. Still, confirm where the excursion departs from, when the river portion begins and how long the return journey takes. These details affect the evening dinner and other plans for the day.

## Tips for exploring the delta

It can be windy on the water, and weather conditions may differ from those in central Buenos Aires. A light windbreaker, sunscreen, hat and sturdy-soled shoes for boarding are useful. A protective phone case and some spare time for walking between piers also help.

If traveling with children or people who need assistance boarding, agree on suitable transport and excursion arrangements in advance. No specific accessibility provisions are separately stated for this excursion, so they should be confirmed individually.

## Frequently asked questions about the Tigre tour

### How long does the Paraná Delta excursion last?

The standalone [Tigre excursion](/argentina/tigre/tigre-parana-delta-half-day-lunch/) takes half a day. On the six-day journey, it is scheduled for the morning of day three.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Lunch, tickets and a guide are included in the excursion. Drinks are included only if agreed separately.

### Can you visit the delta and Buenos Aires on one journey?

Yes. The [six-day tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/) combines activities in the capital with a visit to Tigre.

### Is this a separate multi-day river expedition?

No. The excursion introduces the delta in half a day; the rest of the trip is devoted to other experiences in Argentina.

## Excursions in Tilcara: ancient Pucará and the road through the Humahuaca Gorge

Tilcara lies in Jujuy Province in northwestern Argentina. The town sits in the Río Grande valley among dry mountain slopes and large cacti. Travelers are drawn above all by archaeological sites and the opportunity to visit several settlements in the [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/) on one journey.

Tilcara is included in our ["Humahuaca Gorge, Seven Colors Hill and Inca Cueva" excursion](/argentina/quebrada-de-humahuaca/humahuaca-seven-colours-inca-cueva/). It also visits Purmamarca, Uquía, Humahuaca town and Inca Cueva. Tilcara is an important stop for its pre-Columbian heritage, while the excursion as a whole introduces different periods in the gorge's history.

## What you will see during a stop in Tilcara

The main site is Pucará de Tilcara, an ancient settlement on elevated ground. Stone walls, building foundations and pathways help visitors imagine the lives of local communities before the Spanish conquest. Archaeological research links the site to a settlement that developed from the thirteenth century and later underwent changes under Inca rule. Some structures were reconstructed in the twentieth century, a point worth remembering when looking at the masonry and terraces.

Pucará is often called a fortress. It is more accurate for visitors to understand it as an archaeological complex where people lived, worked, performed rituals and used an established network of Andean routes. The site also overlooks the surrounding valley; the geography helps explain why settlements developed along the river.

If you want an in-depth exploration of the town itself, visit the separate [Tilcara page](/argentina/place/tilcara/). It describes the destination; this catalog focuses on excursion choices and how much of the day a visit takes.

## Why combine Tilcara with other stops?

The Quebrada de Humahuaca is on the UNESCO World Heritage List as a cultural landscape. For thousands of years, the valley linked high Andean areas with the lowlands. Its architecture and settlements are therefore best explored in sequence, rather than as isolated photographic stops.

Our excursion brings together:

- [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/): colorful mountain slopes and geological scenery;
- [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/): the ancient Pucará settlement and archaeological history;
- [Uquía](/argentina/place/uquia/): a colonial church and the artistic tradition of the "Arquebusier Angels";
- [Humahuaca town](/argentina/place/humahuaca/): old streets and historic surroundings.

All these places form part of one Ada Tours excursion. They are not four separate excursions with different prices and departure times. A walk through Pucará, additional time in Tilcara and museum visits depend on the actual itinerary and duration of the stop.

## How much time to allow and how to prepare

Tilcara sits at approximately 2,465 meters above sea level. Travelers who have just arrived from lowlands should walk at a comfortable pace and allow time for climbs along uneven paths. Altitude, dry air and bright sun are noticeable even on a short visit. Bring comfortable closed shoes, drinking water, sun protection and an extra warm layer for the evening.

Argentina's tourism portal recommends several days in Tilcara for independent visits to its museums and surroundings. A sightseeing drive through the gorge serves another purpose: covering the key regional stops on one route. Confirm the exact time at Pucará, opening hours and admission arrangements for your chosen date.

Plan mountain road travel in northwestern Argentina with extra time. Summer rainfall and road conditions may affect journeys, while in the dry season the contrast between sunny days and chilly evenings is particularly noticeable.

## Choosing an excursion that visits Tilcara

If the history of Andean settlements interests you, choose the [Humahuaca Gorge excursion](/argentina/quebrada-de-humahuaca/humahuaca-seven-colours-inca-cueva/). It combines Tilcara's archaeology, Purmamarca's geological landscapes and Uquía's colonial heritage. The excursion has a Russian-speaking guide and includes the named stops. Do not assume that separate museums, extra free time or other services are included unless specified in the terms.

For a wider journey, compare [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) and [Argentina excursions](/argentina/excursion/). If archaeology and local traditions are your main priorities, explore the [culture and history itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/) as well.

## Frequently asked questions about Tilcara excursions

### Can you visit Pucará de Tilcara on an Ada Tours excursion?

Yes. On our Quebrada de Humahuaca excursion, you stop in Tilcara and discover the ancient Indigenous settlement. Confirm the day's timetable and the possibility of a detailed visit to the complex.

### Are Tilcara and Purmamarca the same place?

No. They are separate settlements in the Humahuaca Gorge. Tilcara is especially notable for the Pucará archaeological complex, while Purmamarca is famous for Seven Colors Hill. Both appear as distinct stops on the Ada Tours itinerary.

### Is the stop suitable for someone without trekking experience?

Ordinary sightseeing on this itinerary does not specifically require trekking experience. However, the altitude, uneven surfaces and possible climbs call for suitable shoes and an assessment of your ability to cope with exertion. A long mountain hike is not part of this excursion's description.

## Climbing Aconcagua: what to consider before choosing the expedition

This itinerary aims to reach the summit of [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/), the highest mountain in the Andes and South America, rather than just walking through the national park. Reaching the summit requires a gradual ascent and several nights at elevations where the body is under significant strain. When choosing the trip, experience with multi-day mountain hikes, tolerance of altitude, preparation and the ability to follow guides' decisions matter more than how many beautiful locations appear in the schedule.

The expedition begins in [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/), where equipment is checked. The route then passes [Puente del Inca](/argentina/place/puente-del-inca/) and [Confluencia](/argentina/place/confluencia/) on the way to [Plaza de Mulas](/argentina/place/plaza-de-mulas/) base camp. The principal high-altitude stages and summit attempt take place later in the journey. This sequence distinguishes the expedition from a short visit to mountain valleys.

If you want mountain views without attempting the 6,962 m summit, choose a different experience from the [Argentina adventure tours catalog](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/). The product described here involves a complete high-altitude climbing expedition.

## Acclimatization: why the itinerary includes descents

Participants first hike to Confluencia at about 3,300 m, then climb toward [Plaza Francia](/argentina/place/plaza-francia/) at approximately 4,000 m before descending to sleep lower. After reaching Plaza de Mulas at 4,260 m, an acclimatization hike to [Cerro Bonete](/argentina/place/cerro-bonete/) at around 5,090 m is scheduled, with a return to base camp.

The following stages also proceed gradually: carrying equipment to Camp Canadá, spending a night there, continuing to [Nido de Cóndores](/argentina/place/nido-de-condores/), ascending toward Berlin-Colera, and returning to recover. This gives the body time to adjust. Even so, the acclimatization schedule cannot eliminate altitude sickness or guarantee that an ascent can continue.

| Stage | Purpose on the route |
|---|---|
| Confluencia | Start of the hiking ascent |
| Plaza Francia | Higher acclimatization climb followed by descent |
| Plaza de Mulas | Base camp and recovery |
| Bonete | Acclimatization around 5,100 m |
| Canadá and Nido | Successive nights at altitude |
| Berlin-Colera | Preparation for the summit attempt |

The exact altitude of a camp and the pace of the climb may change with mountain conditions. Decisions to continue depend on weather and the group's condition.

## Who carries the load: mules, porters and participants

Mules transport belongings on the approach to intermediate camps. This lets participants carry a lighter daypack during the early stages. Higher up, arrangements change: each climber carries their own personal gear, while porters assist with group equipment, including tents and kitchen supplies.

We provide one porter for every three clients and up to 20 kg of load per stage. This refers to a share of the group's load, not complimentary transport of all one traveler's personal belongings. A dedicated personal porter costs extra. This distinction is particularly important when assessing the physical demands above Plaza de Mulas.

Before the trip, guides check personal equipment in Mendoza and help participants locate missing items for rental or purchase. However, mountain boots, suitable clothing, sleeping bags and personal gear are not included in the tour price. Agree on an equipment list and acceptable pack weight for each high-altitude stage beforehand.

## Why reaching the summit is not guaranteed even on the full itinerary

The main plan includes a summit attempt after a night at the upper camp. [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) is known, however, for strong winds and rapidly changing weather. Slope conditions, visibility and participants' health may require turning back earlier or postponing the attempt. This is a safety decision.

The 20-day expedition includes two reserve days. They are intended for circumstances that disrupt the normal route. They should not be treated as additional city rest days or guaranteed repeat summit attempts. Confirm where contingency time falls and how delays will be handled before buying international flights.

Guides may change the expedition stages for safety reasons. Paying for the journey does not constitute a promise of reaching the summit.

## What's included and what you should budget for separately

Our expedition includes mountain guides, meals according to the itinerary, mule transport on the specified stages, transfers Mendoza–Puente del Inca–Mendoza, and two nights in a four-star hotel in Mendoza with breakfast and double occupancy. The main program also describes group porters, tent accommodation and communications between camps.

Extra costs include the climbing permit, personal insurance covering a high-altitude expedition, personal equipment and a sleeping bag, additional nights and expenses outside the itinerary. **The Aconcagua permit and appropriate insurance are not included in the tour price.** Mendoza provincial authorities set permit and admission rules for each season; check the park's current procedure and insurance terms when preparing to travel.

When budgeting, it is helpful to separate the expedition price, mandatory individual expenses and a reserve for possible changes to return travel arrangements. This gives a fuller comparison than the headline price alone.

## Assessing your own readiness

Start by considering your previous altitude experience and capacity for sustained multi-day exertion. On this program, you will walk over mountain terrain on consecutive days, sleep in tents at high elevations and carry your own equipment. Good physical fitness at sea level is no substitute for experience adapting to altitude.

Before departure, consider a medical assessment with a doctor familiar with high-altitude activity. Discuss previous climbs, required gear and medical evacuation coverage with the organizer. On the mountain, follow guides' instructions, especially if you feel unwell. A general tourist description is not an appropriate basis for self-prescribing altitude medication.

For more regional geography, seasonal information and other journeys, see the [Argentina guide](/argentina/) and [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/). On this expedition, the key factors remain the altitude schedule, complete equipment and actual permit requirements.

## Frequently asked questions about climbing Aconcagua

### Is this trekking or a summit attempt?

It is an expedition with a planned attempt to reach the 6,962 m summit. Acclimatization hikes and several high camps are included. In adverse conditions, the guiding team decides whether to continue.

### Do I have to carry all my baggage?

Mules carry a substantial part of the load on the early stages. Higher up, participants carry their own gear while porters handle group equipment. Additional transport of personal gear costs extra.

### Are the permit and insurance included?

No. The climbing permit and personal Aconcagua insurance are expressly excluded from the price. Check requirements and coverage before traveling for the relevant season and nationality.

### Why are reserve days included?

They provide time for weather and other circumstances affecting safety and the feasibility of the route. They are a contingency, not a guarantee of a summit attempt or financial compensation if stages change.
